intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, Recent crypto scams, including a NT$5 billion fraud and address poisoning attacks, underscore persistent security risks. North Korean hackers now deploy AI-generated malware against blockchain developers, demanding vigilant innovation.

top_signals.title: 9 detained in NT$5 billion crypto fraud affecting nearly 1,000 victims
top_signals.summary: Nine individuals were detained in Taiwan for their roles in a sophisticated cryptocurrency scam that defrauded nearly 1,000 victims, primarily retail investors including retirees, of over NT$5 billion (US$158 million) across several years. The operation lured victims via social media ads promising high returns on fake crypto tokens like MoChange Token and involved money laundering through real estate and hidden cash. This case underscores escalating cybercrime risks in Taiwan's crypto sector, prompting stricter AML regulations for virtual asset service providers with fines up to NT$5 million and potential imprisonment. Institutional investors should note the Financial Supervisory Commission's push for VASP licensing and a 2026 stablecoin framework to enhance market integrity and investor protections.

top_signals.title: Crypto Investor Loses Over $12 Million in Ethereum to ‘Address Poisoning’ Scam
top_signals.summary: A crypto investor lost $12.4 million in Ether due to an address poisoning scam where the attacker spoofed the victim's wallet address. This highlights the ongoing security risks within the cryptocurrency space.

top_signals.title: KONNI-Gruppe setzt KI-generierte Schadsoftware gegen Blockchain-Entwickler ein
top_signals.summary: North Korean hackers are using AI to create sophisticated malware targeting blockchain developers. The KONNI group is reportedly behind this new tactic.

top_signals.title: Weekend crypto market crash erases $100B as Israel strikes Gaza with ETH and XRP leading losses
top_signals.summary: The crypto market experienced a significant crash over the weekend, erasing $100 billion in value. ETH and XRP led the losses, triggered by geopolitical tensions with Israel striking Gaza.

top_signals.title: I Escaped Chinese Mafia Crypto Slavery
top_signals.summary: A computer engineer from India was trapped in a forced labor operation in Laos, where he was forced to lure Western victims into fake crypto investments. He contacted WIRED journalist Andy Greenberg and exposed the operation before escaping.

top_signals.title: Investors Pull Nearly $818 Million From Bitcoin ETFs as Cryptocurrency Tanks
top_signals.summary: Bitcoin ETFs experienced a significant outflow of $818 million on January 29 as Bitcoin's price dropped. This pushed January into a net negative zone, although cumulative net inflows since inception remain substantial at $55.52 billion.

linkedin_post: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, In the fast-evolving world of Web3, recent headlines serve as stark reminders of the risks we must navigate together. In Taiwan, authorities detained nine individuals behind a massive NT$5 billion crypto fraud that targeted nearly 1,000 victims, including retirees, through fake tokens like MoChange and social media promises of high returns. Funds were laundered via real estate and hidden cash, highlighting the urgent need for stronger AML measures, VASP licensing, and a forthcoming 2026 stablecoin framework to protect investors and build market integrity. Equally alarming, a crypto investor fell victim to an "address poisoning" scam, losing $12.4 million in Ethereum when attackers spoofed their wallet address. This incident underscores persistent security vulnerabilities that demand vigilant wallet practices and advanced protection tools from developers. Adding to these threats, North Korean hackers from the KONNI group are now deploying AI-generated malware specifically against blockchain developers, escalating tactics to breach codebases and steal sensitive data. We empower founders building compliant, resilient solutions in DeFi, tokenized assets, and beyond.
